links.outcome: Ground truth quality for LLM trial screening evaluation
links.effect: Manually annotated data served as ground truth; no assessment of annotator independence or adjudication reported in the abstract.
links.quote: Manually annotated data served as the ground truth.

links.outcome: Comparison of GPT-3.5 vs GPT-4 and prompting approaches on the same data
links.effect: GPT-4 median criterion accuracy 0.838 vs GPT-3.5 0.761; GPT-4 generally outperformed GPT-3.5 but at higher cost ($0.15–$0.27 vs $0.02–$0.03) and time (7.9–12.4 vs 1.4–3 min).
links.quote: LLM performance varies by prompt, with GPT-4 generally outperforming GPT-3.5, but at higher costs and longer processing times.

links.outcome: Patient-level identification of trial-eligible patients meeting all criteria
links.effect: Strict eligibility accuracy only 0.611 (GPT-3.5 SO+EG) and 0.65 (GPT-4 CoT+EG); proportional eligibility AUC up to 0.82.
links.quote: LLMs can be used to identify specific clinical trial criteria but had difficulties identifying patients who met all criteria.
